title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 30
byline: At least 30 people have been killed after a mound of rubbish at a major waste site collapsed on to nearby homes in Guinea’s capital Conakry, the government has said.

title: What’s in the Imran Khan letter? Sunil Gavaskar, Arjuna and others make three key requests
byline: Former captains Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev, Arjuna Ranatunga and Nasser Hussain are among 21 former international cricket captains who have written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, asking for proper medical treatment and welfare of jailed former Pakistan Prime Minister and World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.

title: England hit by fresh discipline storm after Carse incident
byline: England are facing another off-field controversy after fast bowler Brydon Carse was pictured in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby.

title: Reservoirs under pressure as water levels remain low
byline: The country’s major reservoirs are showing worrying variations in water storage, with several tanks recording critically low effective storage levels amid continuing concerns over water availability.

title: Lankan labour migration out to prevent foreign investment: Ravi K
byline: Whilst highlighting that around 300,000 Sri Lankan workers have migrated during the last few years, opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake said over the weekend that this could create new issues.

title: Sergeant loses toe after foreign university Professor’s car runs over his foot
byline: A 63-year-old professor at the University of Cambridge has been arrested after a car he was driving allegedly ran over the toes of a police sergeant who was directing traffic during the Kandy Esala Perahera.

title: SJB MP Chaminda Wijesiri granted bail
byline: Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) MP Chaminda Wijesiri, who was sentenced to 18 months in prison for threatening and assaulting two police officers, has been granted bail by the Badulla High Court pending his appeal.

title: Life in place of death? New plan heads to Cabinet
byline: Despite renewed attention to capital punishment at a high-level anti-narcotics meeting chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, the government is now preparing to submit a Cabinet paper proposing a formal framework that would include commuting death sentences to life imprisonment, reducing life sentences to 20 years and allowing home leave for eligible prisoners.

title: No competitive pricing advantage despite liberalisation of oil trade
byline: Despite somewhat liberalisation of retail oil selling, Sri Lanka is yet to secure the advantage of competitive pricing of petroleum products for its consumers.

title: Jaiswal hits back at Harsha Bhogle over clash with Asitha Fernando
byline: Yashasvi Jaiswal minced no words as he made a sharp attack on Harsha Bhogle over his remarks on Jaiswal’s confrontation with Asitha Fernando during the opening day of the second Test in Colombo,

title: Extreme weather events: advanced alert system not yet in place
byline: In the wake of frequency of seismic jolts in the Indonesian region with tsunami warnings and other forms of extreme weather events, Sri Lanka is yet to activate an automatic mobile alert system for warnings on all kinds of disasters such as Cyclone Ditwah, Daily Mirror learns.

title: Lankan drug lord questioned by FBI over Iran links before deportation
byline: While Sri Lankan authorities continue to investigate notorious drug trafficker Shiran Basik’s alleged drug empire, illicit assets and international links, the Daily Mirror learns that Basik was also questioned in Dubai by FBI agents over possible connections to Iran before he was eventually handed over to Sri Lankan authorities.

title: Top Oman diplomat due in Tehran for talks on Hormuz, Iran says
byline: Oman’s Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi will visit Tehran on Tuesday to continue talks between Iran and Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei says.

title: UN welcomes Sri Lanka’s efforts to bring back refugees from India
byline: The United Nations on Saturday welcomed Sri Lanka’s decision to simplify immigration procedures to expedite the voluntary return of refugees from India who left the country without valid documents during its decades-long civil war.

title: Nearly 3 million Teslas recalled in China over hidden door handles
byline: Minimalist retractable door handles became a signature feature of electric vehicles (EVs), but the controversial designs are now at the centre of China’s biggest car recall, affecting more than 4 million vehicles.

title: Missing Badulla Hospital specialist doctor found dead in Mahiyanganaya
byline: The body of a specialist doctor attached to the Badulla Teaching Hospital, who had been reported missing, was found today (24) on a rock in the Mapakadawewa area of Mahiyanganaya.

title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 30
byline: At least 30 people have been killed after a mound of rubbish at a major waste site collapsed on to nearby homes in Guinea’s capital Conakry, the government has said.

title: Anuradhapura supermarket fined Rs. 200,000 over uncertified electrical cords
byline: The Anuradhapura Magistrate’s Court has imposed a fine of Rs. 200,000 on a supermarket in Anuradhapura for displaying electrical cord reels for sale without the required Sri Lanka Standards (SLS) certification.

title: Parliamentary Committee consults police on reducing prison overcrowding
byline: The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has decided to obtain the views and proposals of the Police Department on measures that could be taken to reduce overcrowding in prisons.

title: SLPP to strengthen grassroots campaign ahead of elections: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa said the party would strengthen its grassroots engagement by visiting communities across the country as it prepares for future elections.

title: PUCSL sets higher solar-storage payments
byline: The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) has introduced higher feed-in tariffs for renewable energy projects equipped with battery storage, as the authorities seek to add at least 450MW of solar PV and battery energy storage capacity to the national electricity system by March next year.

title: Eric Meyer arrives to take up U.S. Ambassador post
byline: U.S. Ambassador-designate to Sri Lanka Eric Meyer arrived in Colombo to assume his duties as the 29th United States Ambassador to Sri Lanka.

title: BASL President, Secretary file petition against 22nd Amendment
byline: The President and Secretary of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) filed a Special Determination petition before the Supreme Court today seeking a declaration that the proposed “Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution” requires approval by the people at a referendum, arguing that the Bill threatens the independence of the Judiciary and the sovereignty of the people.

title: Oil falls as US prepares to unveil new Iran sanctions
byline: Oil prices slipped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits ‌ahead of an expected announcement from Washington about imposing more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East.

title: ICC confirm sanctions for Jaiswal and Asitha Fernando
byline: India batter Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka bowler Asitha Fernando have been sanctioned by the ICC following their incident on the opening day of the second ICC World Test Championship fixture in Colombo.

title: Audit exposes massive Parliament fuel irregularities
byline: A special audit covering the 8th and 9th Parliaments has uncovered a series of irregularities involving fuel allocations, vehicle privileges and expenditure related to several senior parliamentary positions, including the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman of Committees and Secretary-General of Parliament.

title: New Zealand to ban social media for under-16s
byline: New Zealand’s government introduced legislation on Monday to ban under 16s from using social media, joining a number of countries seeking to keep youngsters off sites such as Instagram and TikTok.

title: Sri Lanka moves to introduce digital air cargo community system
byline: The Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation has launched a new initiative to introduce an Air Cargo Community System (ACCS) aimed at making Sri Lanka’s air cargo operations faster, more efficient and transparent.

title: Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
byline: President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new ​H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts.

title: 2027 school exam dates announced
byline: The Examinations Department has announced the dates for the major school examinations scheduled to be held in 2027.

title: CCTV helps swiftly arrest bag thief at Pettah bus stand
byline: A suspect who allegedly stole a passenger’s bag at the Pettah bus stand was swiftly arrested with the assistance of CCTV surveillance, Sri Lanka Air Force personnel said.

title: Heavy crossings drive CSE turnover to LKR 16.85 Bn as ASPI falls below 21,350
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange opened the week on a weaker note on Monday, 24 August 2026, with both benchmark indices closing lower amid broad-based selling pressure.

title: Are our banks losing credibility and public confidence?
byline: An alleged $1 billion money-laundering scheme executed through “phantom imports” has shattered confidence in Sri Lanka’s banking sector. With 13 banks under investigation for processing thousands of fraudulent transactions, the scandal exposes severe breakdowns in basic Know Your Customer protocols and real-time Customs integration. Uncovering this vast network of shell companies proves that compliance cannot remain a mere paper-pushing exercise.

title: Cut thermal power to stabilise electricity tariffs: PUCSL
byline: Electricity tariff fluctuations could be minimised if Sri Lanka reduces its reliance on thermal power generation and increases the use of renewable energy sources, Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) Chairman K. P. L. Chandralal said.
